title: TS SDK: demultiplexer adapter to unify AsyncIterator and Web Streams consumers
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Implement a robust 'demultiplexer' adapter in the TypeScript SDK that allows a single streaming response to be consumed by either an AsyncIterator consumer or a Web Streams consumer (ReadableStream) interchangeably, with correct semantics for backpressure, cancellation, retries, and resumable delivery. Background: customers use a mix of runtimes (Node, Deno, browsers) and consumption patterns. Existing helper code duplicates logic, leaks cancellation semantics, or forces one interface over the other. This ticket produces a single canonical adapter with examples and tests.
non_goals: Do not change transport protocol or server-side streaming format. This adapter is a client-side ergonomic primitive only. No production rollout to Python/Go SDKs in this ticket; those are future follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: A TypeScript API that exports createDemuxStream(responseStream, options) returning { asyncIterator, readableStream }
Backpressure coordination: consuming only one of the surfaces respects upstream demand (no uncontrolled buffering) measured by unit tests and a benchmark script
Cancellation: aborting either surface cancels underlying request and releases resources; cancellation propagates in both directions
Retry-friendly: adapter supports a resumable checkpoint token so callers can request retry without duplicating already-delivered data
Cross-environment: works in Node (ReadableStream polyfilled), Deno, and modern browsers; example usage for each environment included
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering edge cases (concurrent consumers, slow consumer + fast producer, abort then retry) and test vectors included in the PR
design_notes: API shape: createDemuxStream(source: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> | ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, opts?) => { asyncIterator: AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array>, readableStream: ReadableStream<string | Uint8Array>, checkpoint(): string | null }

Buffering strategy: bounded internal queue (configurable default 8 chunks) to smooth pull vs push differences; once queue high-water mark reached, pause upstream (call underlying pause API / backpressure hook) or apply request-level flow control

Backpressure bridging: use a TransformStream inside the ReadableStream path; have the AsyncIterator pull from the same queue; normalize chunks to a canonical envelope {data, seq, checkpoint} internally
Cancellation: a shared AbortController coordinates cancels from either consumer; ensure cleanup of event listeners, clearing queue, & releasing underlying socket

Retries & checkpointing: server may emit checkpoints (opaque strings). The adapter exposes last checkpoint to callers via checkpoint(); caller can include it when retrying. If no server checkpoints, use last sequence number as fallback

Multi-consumer semantics: only one consumer should actively drain at a time; the adapter supports a 'handoff' method for migrating from iterator to stream or vice versa while preserving ordering and not re-emitting chunks

Edge cases: concurrent next() calls from iterator should be serialized; if both surfaces are used concurrently, surface behavior is documented (prefer single active consumer; otherwise the adapter will throw to avoid duplication)
implementation_tasks: Extract canonical chunk envelope and serialization helpers
Implement bounded queue with backpressure signaling to underlying transport
Build ReadableStream wrapper (uses TransformStream where available) and iterator wrapper that read from same queue
Expose checkpoint() and handoff() APIs and wire AbortController for coordinated cancellation
Add environment shims for Node/Deno browser differences and update SDK packaging to include polyfill hints
Write unit tests for all acceptance criteria and an integration test using the local dev server playback harness
Create three usage examples (Node: async iterator for CLI app; Browser: ReadableStream for fetch-and-pipe to <video>/textarea; Hybrid: serverless function using handoff API)
testing_plan: Unit tests: simulate producer emitting bursts and verify consumer behavior under slow iteration and quick stream reads
Integration: run the adapter against the local streaming test harness that can inject network stalls, transient errors, and checkpoint tokens
Load test: micro-benchmark that simulates 1k concurrent small streams to validate memory and queue sizing defaults
Fuzz inputs: malformed chunk frames and missing checkpoint fields to ensure adapter fails gracefully
E2E example validation: run the three usage examples in CI (Node 20, Deno latest, Chromium headless)
rollout_plan: Merge to canary branch behind feature flag ts_demux_adapter
Publish experimental package @redwood/sdk-stream-demuxer@canary and post to internal slack for SDK devs
Collect usage/bug reports for 2 weeks, then merge to main and include in ts-sdk-1.12 release notes
Write docs and examples in SDK docs site and mark feature stable after no regressions in 30 days
open_questions: Should checkpoint be an opaque string only, or also support structured JSON that the SDK can interpret? Prefer opaque for now, but check ops requirements
If underlying transport does not support explicit pause/resume, should adapter buffer more aggressively or surface a 'no backpressure support' label?
Handoff semantics: do we support soft-copying state to allow two consumers with shared read offset (rare) or deny by throwing? Prefer deny for simplicity
Do we need to expose a statistics hook (queue length, avg latency) for Console observability? Could be separate ticket
comments: 2025-02-10 Sofia Martinez: Initial ticket and design outline. I sketched the API shape and basic queue semantics. Assigned to Linus for implementation.

2025-02-11 Linus Kwan: Spike completed — validated TransformStream approach in Chromium and Node with web-streams-polyfill. Observed that unbounded buffering in Node quickly increases memory; implemented bounded queue and simple backpressure hook; pushing tests next.

2025-02-12 Asha Patel (review): Design looks good. Two suggestions: (1) expose lastCheckpoint() rather than checkpoint() to avoid name clash with server API, and (2) add a small TTL for checkpoint retention to avoid holding state for long-lived idle streams. Added as followups.
2025-02-13 Linus Kwan: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/9623 — includes adapter and basic tests. Needs review for error semantics when both surfaces are used concurrently.

2025-02-14 QA Bot: Integration test run showed a flake where aborting the iterator did not close the ReadableStream in Node 18; added a shim to ensure proper stream closed callback. Re-running full suite.

2025-02-15 Sohini Rao (PM): Marking feature as high priority for next minor release due to enterprise customers asking for clearer streaming ergonomics. Please capture migration notes in docs before merging.
notes_for_docs: Add migration guide showing common patterns: iterator-only apps, stream-only apps, and handoff migration. Include examples of retry using lastCheckpoint() and recommended queue_size defaults.
follow_up_tasks: Create python and go parity tickets for equivalent adapters
Add observability metrics export for queue length and dropped-chunks
Consider adding structured checkpoint support after ops alignment
